description: Tabulation is a systematic process of organizing data into rows and columns. It is a crucial part of Data Interpretation in competitive exams, aiding in quick analysis and comparison.

sections.title: Basics of Tables
sections.description: Understanding the structure of a table and the data it contains is the first step to solving questions.

key_concepts.explanation: A horizontal arrangement of data that typically represents a specific subject, entity, or time period.
A vertical arrangement of data that represents different categories or parameters.

sections.title: Essential Mathematical Formulas
sections.description: Basic calculations used to quickly solve table-based questions.

equations: Percentage of x w.r.t y = (x / y) * 100
Average = (Sum of all terms) / (Total number of terms)

sections.title: Steps to Solve Questions
sections.description: A systematic approach to ensure accuracy and speed during exams.

steps.title: Read Title and Units
steps.detail: Read the table's title and check if the values are given in thousands, millions, ratios, or percentages.

steps.title: Scan the Data
steps.detail: Quickly glance over the entire table to understand what the data is about. Carefully read any footnotes provided below.

steps.title: Use Approximation
steps.detail: Instead of exact calculations, look at the options and find approximate values to save time.

sections.title: Specific Cases and Question Types
sections.description: Typical table patterns frequently asked in examinations.

results: Calculating the direct ratio of values from two different columns or rows.
Finding unknown values by establishing equal proportions.
Calculating unknown values from other given information (like total sum, average).
Filling in the blanks using additional data provided within the questions.
